follow-up time: Women were followed up at 20 weeks and 28-30 weeks for the development of PAS.
exposure: LUS scar location in relation to the CIC (within or above)
LUS scar location in relation to the cervicoisthmic canal (CIC) (within or above)
lower uterine segment (LUS) scar size (narrow or dehiscent)
Risk of PAS based on the relationship between scar location and placental site
cohort: 535 women with a history of Cesarean section (CS) at 11-13 weeks' gestation
finding: Routine transvaginal ultrasound assessment of the location of the lower uterine segment scar and placenta at the time of first-trimester screening between 11 + 0 and 13 + 6 weeks' gestation in women with prior CS is a feasible and effective tool to identify those at risk of subsequent development of PAS disorder.
